General Procedure 3: Screening of aryl halide, iron salt and ligand
In an argon-filled glovebox, an oven dried 7.5 mL vial was charged with the appropriate iron salt (0.02
M in THF, 0.5 mL, 0.01 mmol) and the appropriate ligand or ligand precursor (0.01 mmol), the resulting
mixture was allowed to stir at rt for 30 min. MgBr2·OEt2 (0.2 mL, 0.1 M in THF, 0.02 mmol), aryl halide
1 (0.1 mmol) and aryl boronate 2a (0.5 mL, 0.4 M in THF, 0.2 mmol) were then added to the vial
sequentially. The reaction mixture was then heated to 80 °C and stirred for 18 h. The resulting mixture
was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (1.0 mL) before dodecane (internal
standard, 22.7 µL, 0.1 mmol) was added and the reaction mixture extracted into CH2Cl2 (5.0 mL). After
being thoroughly stirred, an aliquot was then taken and filtered through Celite (eluting with CH2Cl2)
and was then analysed by GC.

General Procedure 4: Screening of boronic esters
Under an N2 atmosphere, an oven dried Schlenk tube was charged with the appropriate boronic ester
(0.5 mmol) and then THF (3.0 mL) and the resultant solution cooled to -40 °C. tBuLi (0.29 mL, 1.7 M in
hexane, 0.5 mmol) was then added dropwise and the resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 mins at
-40 °C. The reaction mixture was slowly brought to rt and stirred for a further 45 mins.
Meanwhile, in an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (8.6 mg, 0.025 mmol) and FeBr3 (7.4 mg, 0.025
mmol) were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by THF (1.5 mL), and the
resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 min at rt. MgBr2·OEt2 (12.9 mg, 0.05 mmol) and chlorobenzene
1a (25.5 µL, 0.25 mmol) were then added. The Schlenk tube was sealed and taken out of the glovebox
and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to an external temperature of 80 °C. The aryl boronate
formed in situ above was then added in one portion, the Schlenk was sealed, and the reaction mixture
was heated at 80 °C for 18 h. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched
with 1.0 M HCl (2.5 mL) and dodecane (internal standard, 56.8 µL, 0.25 mmol) was added. The organics
were extracted into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken for analysis by GC.

General Procedure 5: Screening of temperature and solvents
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (8.6 mg, 0.025 mmol) and FeBr3 (7.4 mg, 0.025 mmol) were
added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by the appropriate solvent (1.5 mL),
and the resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 min at rt. MgBr2·OEt2 (12.9 mg, 0.05 mmol) and
chlorobenzene 1a (25.5 µL, 0.25 mmol) were then added. In a separate Schlenk tube the aryl boronate
2a (221.1 mg, 0.5 mmol) was dissolved in the appropriate solvent (1.5 mL). Both Schlenk tubes were
sealed and taken out of the glove box, attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the appropriate
temperature whilst the reaction mixtures were stirred. The aryl boronate containing solution was then
added quickly to the Schlenk containing the other reaction components, the Schlenk was sealed, and
the resultant mixture was heated at the temperature shown in Supplementary Table 7, and stirred
for 18 h. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (2.5
mL) and dodecane (internal standard, 56.8 µL, 0.25 mmol) was added. The organics were extracted
into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken to be analysed by GC.

mixture was stirred for 30 min at rt, during which time an orange suspension formed. MgBr2·OEt2 (51.6
mg, 0.2 mmol) and chlorobenzene 1a (102 µL, 1.0 mmol) were then added. In a separate Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (884.7 mg, 2.0 mmol) was dissolved in 2-MeTHF (6.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the

In order, to determine the best functional for the single point energy calculation of all the structures
examined in the catalytic manifolds we undertook a benchmarking study based on the simplified
model compounds SM1-4 in all available spin states (Supplementary Figure 61) using Orca 5.0.3. The
geometries for each model in each spin state were optimized using the BP86 functional with a D3BJ
dispersion correction and the def2-TZVP basis set and a frequency calculation was performed at the
same level of theory. The optimised cartesian coordinates are given below. Reference energies for
each of the models were calculated using dlpno-CCSD(T1) which employs an improved iterative
approximation for the perturbative triple excitations.59 The calculations were based on the orbitals
derived for the BP86 optimiations, using def-TZVP basis sets and relativistic effects were accounted
for using the ZORA approximation.60-62 Two calculations were performed for each species, using the
TightPNO default parameters except for the TCutPNO thresholds which were set to 1e-5 and 1e-6 in the
two calculations, which allowed two point (5,6) extrapolation to the PNO space limit.63,64
Next single point calculations were performed on the BP86-optimised model structures in all possible
spin states using the functionals BP86, TPPSh, wB97X, B3LYP, TPSS0, PBE0, PW6B95, PBE0-1/3, BB1K,
mPWB1K, B2PLYP, mPW2PLYP, M06 and M06-2X and the def2-TZVP basis set. In all cases except PBE0-
1/3, BB1K, mPW2PLYP, M06 and M06-2X the D3BJ dispersion correction was applied. The PW6B95,
PBE0-1/3, BB1K and mPWB1K functionals were obtained from LibXC.65 The single point electronic
energies obtained by the coupled-cluster and DFT methods are summarised in Supplementary Figure
61. In all cases, the dlpno-CCSD(T1) calculations predict high spin (HS) ground states. While all of the
functionals tested also predicted the ground state for the Fe(0) and Fe(I) models (SM1 and SM2) to be
HS, BP86 and TPSSh predict an intermediate spin (IS) ground state for the Fe(III) model SM4 at variance
with the coupled cluster reference results. Similarly BP86 predicts and IS ground state for the Fe(II)
model SM3. The next lowest energy state predicted by the coupled cluster calculation is intermediate
spin for both Fe(II) and Fe(III) models, except with TPSSh which has the HS and IS of Fe(III) reversed
and BP86 which predicts HS as the second lowest energy spin state for Fe(II) and LS as the second
highest for Fe(III). Examining the data in Supplementary Figure 61 it can be seen that the PBE0
functional gives the lowest unsigned variance from the dlpno-CCSD(T1) reference data (5.2 kcal/mol)
which improves when only the ground state and next lowest energy state data are considered for all
oxidation states (3.3 kcal/mol). In general the functional tested performed poorly against the coupled
cluster reference data for Fe(II) LS with only BB1K and mPWB1K predicting the HS-LS gap to within 5
kcal/mol of the couple cluster value. At this stage we cannot rule out the possibility of the single
reference coupled cluster method is failing to fully capture static correlation energy of what is
intrinsically a multireference system, but note that the T1 diagnostic value (0.025) lies below the cut-
off of 0.05, values above which can indicate substantial static correlation.66 It can be predicted from
simple ligand considerations that low-coordinate Fe(II) complexes with only two strong field ligands
are unlikely to adopt LS configurations. Thus while the calculation of Fe(II) LS electronic states appears
to be problematic for the DFT functionals investigated, the LS Fe(II) pathways considered in the
calculations of the catalytic manifolds are not likely to be relevant.
